temperature, different time: thickness decides how long the heat takes to reach the middle. Portion Air fryer Oven reheat Sliced steak 300°F / 150°C · 4 min 275°F / 135°C · 15 min Whole steak, about 1 inch 300°F / 150°C · 8 min 275°F / 135°C · 30 min Whole steak, about 1½ inches 300°F / 150°C · 11 min 275°F / 135°C · 41 min Safe or pink: two targets that do not meet A steak cooked medium-rare finished at around 120°F inside. USDA guidance for reheating any leftovers is 165°F, and getting the middle of a steak that hot cooks it through to well done. There is no setting that does both, so this page gives you the two numbers and lets you choose. The low temperature is what keeps either choice good: at a gentle heat, the outside does not toughen and grey while the centre is still warming, so the steak heats evenly. The time here is an estimate for a whole steak to reach 165°F, not a tested figure, because thickness and fridge temperature vary. Start checking with a thermometer at the flip and decide from the reading. Worked example: one leftover sirloin A 1-inch sirloin from the night before, out of the fridge. Preheat 3 minutes and heat at 300°F, turning it at 4 minutes and checking the centre then. For the USDA 165°F, expect about 8 minutes in total; a 1½-inch steak takes about 11. Sliced steak is hot through in about 4. In a conventional oven, the slow method is 275°F for around 30 minutes on a rack. How to check it Use an instant-read thermometer in the very centre of the thickest part. At the flip, a reading of 110–120°F means the steak is warm and still pink; carry on to 165°F (74°C) if you follow the USDA leftover guidance. The surface should be sizzling but not dry or curling at the edges. Before it goes in Let the steak sit out while the air fryer heats so the centre is less cold. Brush it with a little oil or butter to keep the surface from drying. Save any juices from the plate and spoon them over before serving. Related presets Steak 400°F · 10 min · flip at 5 Leftover pizza 350°F · 4 min Leftover fries 375°F · 4 min · shake ×1 350°F oven to air fryer, every food → Oven to air fryer converter → All food presets → Printable conversion chart → Frequently asked questions How do I get steak hot through without overcooking it? Slice before reheating if you want it hot through without overcooking. Thin slices reach 165°F in about 4 minutes, before they can turn grey and tough. What temperature should reheated steak reach? USDA guidance for leftovers is 165°F (74°C). Many people stop at 110–120°F to keep it pink; that is your call. Is the time on this page exact? No. It is an estimate for a 1-inch steak from the fridge. Start checking with a thermometer at 4 minutes and go by the reading. Why such a low temperature? A gentle heat warms the centre before the outside dries out, so the steak stays the same colour from edge to middle. How do I reheat steak in the oven? On a rack at 275°F for around 30 minutes, then sear it briefly in a hot pan if you want the crust back. mainEntity.name: How do I get steak hot through without overcooking it?

acceptedAnswer.text: Slice before reheating if you want it hot through without overcooking. Thin slices reach 165°F in about 4 minutes, before they can turn grey and tough.

mainEntity.name: What temperature should reheated steak reach?

acceptedAnswer.text: USDA guidance for leftovers is 165°F (74°C). Many people stop at 110–120°F to keep it pink; that is your call.

mainEntity.name: Is the time on this page exact?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. It is an estimate for a 1-inch steak from the fridge. Start checking with a thermometer at 4 minutes and go by the reading.
A gentle heat warms the centre before the outside dries out, so the steak stays the same colour from edge to middle.

mainEntity.name: How do I reheat steak in the oven?
